issues.failure_explanation: Since \widehat{P} maps into degree-k polynomials, |\hat I-\widehat P\hat I|_{H^{k+1}}=|\hat I|_{H^{k+1}}. The H^{k+1} norm of the projection error is therefore O(1), not O(h^{k+1}). The displayed chain only yields h^{-1/2}\|\hat I\|_{H^{k+1}}, so the claimed h^{k+1/2} trace bound does not follow as written.

issues.failure_explanation: L_4 contains the one-sided trace (\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I)^- on interior faces, while the DG norm contains only jumps there. Counterexample in a 1D analogue: take a uniform mesh, \tilde I=x^{k+1} with k odd. The projection-error jumps vanish, so \|w\|_{DG}\sim h^{k+1}. Yet L_4 can reach h^{k+1/2}\|v_h\|_{DG}, so the ratio blows up like h^{-1/2}. Thus eq3.4 is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \|\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I\|_{DG} by an augmented norm that includes upwind face traces. Bound that norm by h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^{k+1}} via trace inequalities, as in eq3.3.

issues.failure_explanation: Eq3.8 is an error estimate and says nothing about volumes. D_c consists of whole elements touching the characteristic set. In 2D that set is finitely many points, giving O(1) elements of area h^2; in 3D it is a curve of length O(1), giving O(h^{-1}) elements of volume h^3. So Vol(D_c)\sim h^2, which exceeds h^{k+1} for k\ge2. The chain in eq3.25 then gives only T_3\lesssim h^k. A direct estimate gives the same order: on S=\Gamma_h^-\setminus\Phi_h(\Gamma^-) the scheme imposes g_h=0 while \tilde I=O(1), with |\Omega\cdot n_h|\lesssim h^k and Area(S)\lesssim h^k, hence T_3\lesssim h^k\|\tilde I\|_\infty\|v_h\|_{DG}. The k\ge2 restriction and the h^{k+1/2} rate rest on the false volume claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either weaken eq3.18 to O(h^k), or change the inflow-data extension (e.g. a smooth extension of g instead of zero extension) and re-prove that the geometric inflow consistency error is O(h^{k+1/2}).
issues.overall_effect: The main optimal O(h^{k+1/2}) DG estimate eq3.18 is unsupported; the argument yields only O(h^k). The abstract, introduction and conclusion claims of optimal-rate recovery are unsupported to the same extent.
